# NYS DREAM Act Steps to Apply

## Step 1: Determining Your Eligibility

If you fit one of the descriptions below, you may be eligible for one or more NYS student financial aid awards under the DREAM Act:

## Step 2: Completing the Application

Students meeting the NYS DREAM Act eligibility criteria can apply for one or more HESC-administered grant and scholarship programs and be directed to the [NYS DREAM Act application](https://nysdream.applyists.net/) powered by International Scholarship & Tuition Services (ISTS).

The application is simple and straightforward, and the information provided will be used ONLY to determine eligibility for and administer awards.

Applicants without lawful immigration status will NOT be asked for their home address and will NOT have to upload financial records.

## Step 3: Monitoring the Status of Your Application

Once you have submitted an application, it is your responsibility to monitor its status and ensure its completion. After submitting your application, you will be able to upload any required documentation and monitor its status online.

## Step 4: Award Notification and Acceptance

You will be notified by email when a determination has been made regarding your eligibility for each award for which you have applied. If you are determined to be eligible for an award, your next step will be to accept the award!

For certain awards, you must sign a contract agreeing to live and/or work in New York State for a required number of years after graduation as a condition of receiving the award. If you decide not to accept an award with a post-graduation requirement, please indicate this on the contract.

### Terms to Know

**Temporary Protected Status (TPS)**: foreign nationals to remain in the U.S. if during the time they were in the U.S. something catastrophic happened in their country of origin preventing their safe return – for example war, famine, natural disaster, or epidemic. TPS allows people to work legally and be protected from deportation.

**T-Visa**: Allows the granting of lawful status to noncitizen victims of human trafficking, as well as their immediate family members, who assist in the prosecution of the trafficking. It allows people to remain and work temporarily in the U.S.

**U-Visa**: Allows for the granting of lawful status to noncitizen crime victims who suffered significant physical or mental abuse (and their immediate family members) who assist in the prosecution of the crime. It allows people to remain and work temporarily in the U.S.

**Without Lawful Immigration Status**: Living in the U.S. unlawfully either because lawful status never existed (including those with DACA status) or has ended.

### Need Help?

NYS DREAM Act applicants or recipients can receive support via email at [[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#bff1e6ecfbedfafef2ffdecfcfd3c6f6ecebec91dcd0d2) or chat by logging into your HESC ISTS Student Account.

A safe loan to help cover important expenses

### Credit-building

Payments are reported to all major credit bureaus

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

* About the program
* Getting Started
* Availability

* Is this the same Lending Circles program as MAF’s?

  Yes. Every partner in our network runs the same [Lending Circles program](/lending-circles/): zero-interest loans, credit reporting to all major bureaus, and the same standards of care. The only difference is that you’ll be working with a local nonprofit that knows your community.
* How are these partners vetted?

  Every partner in our network is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit that has gone through MAF’s training and certification process. They follow the same program standards we do — so you can expect the same quality of service no matter which partner you work with.
* What does it cost to participate?

  Lending Circles are zero-interest; there are no fees or interest charges on the loan itself. Check with your local partner for details.
* Will participating affect my credit score?

  Lending Circles reports monthly payments to all three major credit bureaus: Experian, Equifax, and TransUnion. For most participants, this results in a positive impact on their credit score over the course of the program.

* Will my MAF application transfer to the partner?

  For privacy reasons, you’ll need to start a new application directly with the partner organization. The good news: the process is similar to MAF’s, and most partners can get you started right away.
* What documents will I need to apply?

  Requirements vary slightly by partner, but most will ask for a government-issued ID, proof of income, and proof of address. Contact your local partner before your appointment so you can come prepared.
* Do I need a Social Security Number to apply?

  No. Lending Circles welcomes participants regardless of immigration status. An Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN) is accepted in place of a Social Security Number.

* What if there’s no partner in my state yet?

  We're continuing to grow our network across the country. If there's no partner near you right now, tell us your zip code and we'll email you when a partner opens near you. In the meantime, explore Lending Circles and other financial tools available to you.

  + [Learn More About Lending Circles](/lending-circles/)
  + [Want to bring Lending Circles to your community?](/becoming-a-lc-provider/)
* Can I apply directly with MAF instead?

  MAF serves participants primarily in the San Francisco Bay Area. If you’re outside our direct service area, a partner organization is the best way to access Lending Circles near you. If you are in California and want to participate in a Lending Circle with MAF, [start here](/lending-circles/).
* Can my organization become a partner?

  Yes! We’re always looking to grow our network. If your organization is a registered 501(c)(3) and serves a community that could benefit from Lending Circles, learn more about the certification process below.

  + [Want to bring Lending Circles to your community?](/becoming-a-lc-provider/)
